what_is_declared: MIDA: model, inquiry (estimand), data strategy (sampling, assignment incl. clusters and blocks, measurement), answer strategy; fabricatr declares nested and cross-classified levels (add_level, nest_level, cross_levels, link_levels)
required_inputs: A design is R code; diagnosis needs at least one inquiry and an estimator mapped to it
format: R objects (code), not a data file
gap_for_lmecheck: Declares designs for simulation; does not read real data or check a declaration against it; no file format to share with Python. randomizr does check data at assignment time ('All units within a cluster must be in the same block')

what_is_declared: Within and between factors (sim_design), random factors crossed or nested (add_random(..., .nested_in = NULL) crosses by default), random effects (add_ranef), contrasts; design stored as an attribute and exportable with json_design(); codebook() writes Psych-DS 0.1.0 JSON-LD
required_inputs: Factor levels, n, mu, sd, r; column roles only for codebook (identifier, levels, na)
gap_for_lmecheck: check_mixed_design() takes subject and item columns as arguments and fits a null lmer; no inference or checking of structure from data; JSON describes a simulated design, not a dataset
source: cran/faux man/add_random.Rd, man/check_mixed_design.Rd, R/check_mixed_design.R, man/codebook.Rd, man/json_design.Rd

what_is_declared: fixed.factor(); random.factor(name, groups =) declares which fixed or random factors a random factor is nested in; design.formula() derives the maximal lme4 formula (each random factor gets slopes for every fixed factor it is not grouped by)
format: R S4 objects; write.design.json() writes experimental codes, not the design semantics
gap_for_lmecheck: Closest precedent for a declaration-implied maximal structure, but from declared design only; never checks real data

what_is_declared: Structure implied by a fitted (or makeLmer-built) model; extend(along =, within =) names the unit to enlarge and the grouping within which to extend
required_inputs: A fitted lme4 model and its data, or formula plus parameter values
gap_for_lmecheck: No explicit declaration of nesting, randomisation unit or roles; inherits whatever the model frame encodes, including reused labels

what_is_declared: fixed_effects (names), simvar (the random variable to vary), R2power adds a second random variable (R2var, R2level) for crossed designs
required_inputs: A fitted lme4 model, its data, fixed_effects, simvar, steps, critical_value, n_sim
licence: DESCRIPTION says 'GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE' without a version
gap_for_lmecheck: Unit names are declared as arguments but structure is taken from the model; no file format

framework: Frictionless Table Schema / Data Package v2
version_checked: v2.0 released 2024-06-26; R frictionless 2.0.1 (CRAN 2026-10-29); Python frictionless 5.21.0 (PyPI 2026-10-15)
what_is_declared: Field name (required), type and format, constraints, categories and categoriesOrdered (level order), missingValues per table or field (v2: labelled missing values), primaryKey, uniqueKeys, foreignKeys, fieldsMatch; extensions through $schema profiles; field descriptors may carry other properties
gap_for_lmecheck: No notion of nesting semantics, randomisation, roles relative to assignment, time order or estimands. R frictionless 2.0.0 NEWS: field.categories and schema.fieldsMatch not yet supported, so level order would not round-trip through it in R

what_is_declared: Dataset metadata (schema.org Dataset JSON-LD), variableMeasured with descriptions, levels, identifiers, missing codes; file-naming rules; columns must appear in variableMeasured
gap_for_lmecheck: Documents variables, not design relations; validator needs Node.js

version_checked: DDI-CDI 1.0 published January 2025 (DDI Alliance announcement via search)
what_is_declared: CDI data-structure components with roles: identifier, measure, attribute, dimension; Codebook and Lifecycle document variables, universes and analysis units for survey archives
languages: R: DDIwR 0.22 (GPL >= 3) converts data to and from DDI, SPSS, Stata, SAS and R, including user-declared missing values; no Python reader checked
gap_for_lmecheck: Too heavy for a two-language package; offers the identifier/measure/attribute vocabulary only. docs.ddialliance.org was unreachable, so CDI class definitions were read from search snippets only
source: WebSearch snippets of docs.ddialliance.org and ddialliance.org news; cran/DDIwR DESCRIPTION

framework: CONSORT 2010 extension to cluster randomised trials
version_checked: Campbell et al. (2012); CONSORT 2025 core statement (Hopewell et al., 2025); no 2025-aligned cluster extension found
what_is_declared: Reporting items: definition of the cluster and how design features apply to clusters (3a); sample size with number of clusters, cluster size, ICC and its uncertainty (7a); stratification or matching; allocation based on clusters; how clustering was taken into account (12a); results with an ICC for each primary outcome (17a, per checklist copies)
required_inputs: A reporting checklist, not a data format
gap_for_lmecheck: Maps onto declaration fields (units, assignment.unit, assignment.blocks, estimand level) and onto Stream B outputs (ICC needs the outcome: tier T1)
source: WebSearch: PubMed 22951546 listing; Springer supplementary checklist copies; catalogue L7-03 verifier

version_checked: OSF Preregistration; AsPredicted; ESM template (Kirtley et al., 2021); ERP guidelines and template (Paul et al., 2021); machine-readable hypotheses with scienceverse (Lakens & DeBruine, 2021)
what_is_declared: Free-text sections on design, sampling, variables and analysis; the ESM template adds sampling schemes and time-outs; the ERP guidelines add preprocessing steps
gap_for_lmecheck: No template specific to mixed models was found; a search found only general templates and advice to state the formula, random-effects structure and convergence fallback in advance. A hashed declaration plus the Stream B ladder file can be attached to any of them
source: WebSearch results (SFB1252 preregistration talk; APS and KU Leuven records; MPI and COS pages)
